title: Set of bounded-size object isomorphism classes
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] with generator $U$. For an object $M$ of $\mathcal A$ its *size* $|M|$ is the cardinality of the set of subobjects of $M$. Let $\kappa$ be a cardinal. (1) If $|M|\le\kappa$, then $M$ is a quotient of a direct sum of at most $\kappa$ copies of $U$. (2) The isomorphism classes of objects $M$ of $\mathcal A$ with $|M|\le\kappa$ form a set.

proof.text: For every proper subobject $M'\subsetneq M$, the generator property of $U$ gives a morphism $\varphi_{M'}:U\to M$ whose image is not contained in $M'$. The coproduct map $\bigoplus_{M'\subsetneq M}U\to M$ induced by these morphisms is an epimorphism: if its image were contained in a proper subobject $N\subsetneq M$, then the summand indexed by $N$ would have image contained in $N$, contradicting its choice. The index set is the set of proper subobjects of $M$, so it has cardinality at most $|M|\le\kappa$.

For each cardinal $\lambda\le\kappa$, the coproduct $U^{(\lambda)}$ exists by the small-colimit hypothesis in the Grothendieck-abelian definition. By [lem-pur-kinjective-set-of-subobjects], the subobjects of $U^{(\lambda)}$ form a set, and each quotient of $U^{(\lambda)}$ is determined up to isomorphism by the kernel of a quotient map. Since the cardinals $\lambda\le\kappa$ form a set, the union of these sets of quotient isomorphism classes is a set.
By the first step, every object $M$ with $|M|\le\kappa$ is one of the quotients considered in the second step. Therefore the isomorphism classes of all such $M$ form a set.
